summary: Cast-iron lighthouse at the entrance to Port aux Basques harbour, lit in 1875; reachable only by boat, and still an active light.

light.note: Station established 1874 (Rowlett); light not in operation until spring 1875 (LighthouseFriends). Originally a fixed red light.

structures.type: square wooden tower on a wooden base
structures.note: First tower, showing a fixed red light from a 27.5 m focal plane; LighthouseFriends does not say when it was removed

structures.type: cylindrical cast-iron tower, several segments bolted together
structures.note: Date and height disputed: heritage statement 88-037 says built 1874-75 and about 8 m; LighthouseFriends says 1895 and 17 m; Rowlett says 1895 and 11 m

access.note: Accessible only by boat, visible from the mainland and from the ferries (Rowlett); the Lighthouse Digest-era access notes are not checked

events.note: Station established; work on the lighthouse carried out (Rowlett: station established 1874)
Light not put into operation until spring 1875 (LighthouseFriends)
Small keeper's dwelling built beside the tower, after the 1876 inspection
Brick cistern built to collect rainwater; recommended in 1879
Circular cast-iron tower erected beside the wooden tower (LighthouseFriends, Rowlett). The 1988 heritage statement dates the cast-iron tower to 1874-75 (conflict).
Fourth-order lens fitted to the iron tower (LighthouseFriends)
Fog signal building; gun-cotton cartridge fired every eight minutes in fog
Compressed-air diaphone fog alarm replaces the gun-cotton explosives
Light converted from kerosene to electric
Recognized Federal Heritage Building (FHBRO report 88-037; statement of significance)
Keeper's duplex removed; light and fog signal remain active (LighthouseFriends)
Major restoration by the Coast Guard (Rowlett)
April 2016: Coast Guard announced the wharf unsafe and to be removed; access would have been by helicopter only; after protests the wharf was kept
New wharf and walkway built after protests by the Channel Head Heritage Lighthouse Society (Rowlett)

notes_for_editor: 1) TOWER CONFLICT, unresolved. The 1988 FHBRO heritage statement (report 88-037) says the Channel Head lightstation was built in 1874-75 and describes a circular tower about eight metres high, which it says appears to have been fabricated in Britain. LighthouseFriends says the first tower was a square wooden one of 1874-75 (nine metres, fixed red light, focal plane 27.5 m) and that a circular iron tower of 17 m was erected beside it in 1895 with a fourth-order lens. The Lighthouse Directory says the cast-iron tower (11 m) dates from 1895 with the station established 1874. The story gives the statement's date for the lightstation and LighthouseFriends' and the Directory's 1895 date for the iron tower, and says the sources do not agree. The FHBRO building report 88-037 itself was not read; a human should check it, and the Canadian Register's photo caption, before a date is settled. 2) FIRST LIGHT: LighthouseFriends says the light was not put into operation until spring 1875; the record and the Lighthouse Directory give 1874 (station established). The correction is proposed in corrections, not applied. 3) NEWFOUNDLAND was not part of Canada until 1949, so the Canadian Department of Marine reports in the corpus (fiscal 1900 to 1923-24) do not cover this station. Keeper names and dates rest on LighthouseFriends alone. 4) A search of Chronicling America for 'Channel Head' with 'Port aux Basques' (1874-1930) returned no hits. 5) No storms, wrecks or rescues were sourced, so that chapter is omitted. A 1957 storm named in the Lighthouse Directory concerns the Rose Blanche light, not this station. 6) The 1857 remark quoted by LighthouseFriends is unattributed in that source and is not used. 7) ACCESS: the Lighthouse Directory says accessible only by boat, site open, tower closed; LighthouseFriends says grounds open, tower closed. Not checked in person. 8) KEEPERS: E. Pike's first name is not given in any source read. John T. Gillam is from LighthouseFriends alone. 9) The 1988 statement's 'appears' hedge is kept in the story. 10) No photos were added; the record's Wikimedia Commons photo was not checked for licence. 11) COPYRIGHT: LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Directory are copyrighted sites. In the fact-check, their wording was paraphrased and direct quotations removed, except the Coast Guard list and the FHBRO and register text (government sources).
